summary: Voice on a radio wave: FM deviation, double and single sideband, Figure 3H17, the two-tone test, and pulse modulation.

blocks.title: Voice on a carrier
items: Carrier: a steady radio wave from an oscillator. Audio alone needs an antenna many miles long.
Modulation: changing the carrier in step with the audio, the modulating signal.
AM changes the carrier's height. The outline of its peaks, the envelope, is the message.
FM keeps the height steady and swings the frequency. Feed the audio directly to the oscillator, through a varactor or reactance modulator.
Deviation: how far the frequency swings from center, in kHz. Louder audio, bigger deviation.

items.name: Modulation index
items.means: At a given time, so it varies with the audio.

items.name: Deviation ratio
items.means: Design limits, so it's fixed. Modulation rate means audio frequency.

blocks.title: Double and single sideband
items: DSB, double sideband, is ordinary AM. Modulate the supply voltage to a class C amplifier, which works in short bursts.
SSB, single sideband: 1 sideband, carrier suppressed. All the power carries the voice.

blocks.title: Testing SSB
items: Linear amplifier: an exact, bigger copy of its input. SSB's strength follows the voice, so it needs one. Class C won't do.
Two-tone test checks amplitude linearity: a two-tone audio-frequency sine wave in, the output on an oscilloscope.
The tones: 2 non-harmonically related audio signals within the modulation passband, such as about 700 Hz and 1,900 Hz.
Reading it: clean, even loops mean linear. Flat tops or zero-crossing distortion mean non-linear.

blocks.title: Pulses
items: Pulses: short bursts at a steady repetition rate, each carrying a voice sample.
PWM voice: a standard pulse is varied in duration by an amount depending on the voice waveform at that instant.
Average power = peak × duty cycle, the fraction of time it's on: 1000 W × 1/1000 = 1 W. Peak is normally much greater than average.
PCM, pulse-code modulation: each sample becomes a number, sent as on-off pulses. Noise rarely turns on into off.
Time-division multiplex: channels take turns in time slots on 1 frequency. Transmit and receive clock pulse rates must be synchronized.

blocks.title: Exam traps
items: Deviation goes on top. 0.6 and 0.47 are upside down.
Maximum in the wording means deviation ratio, not modulation index.
Varying an amplifier's supply gives AM, not FM.
Audio reaches block 3 but is inserted at block 2.
The two-tone test shows linearity, not phase shift, FM percentage or sideband suppression.
PWM varies duration, not amplitude or frequency. PPM varies time, not pulses per second.
Time-division channels need clock sync, not frequency separation.
